_doc.what: Variant of config-sample.json showing EXTERNAL CLI EXECUTORS: any tier slot can point at a command-line agent (another vendor's CLI) instead of a native model name. Read config-sample.json first for the full key guide.
_doc.contract: A cli-shaped slot is GATHER-ONLY (cli_tier_gather_only): file hunts, scans, reviews, advisor consults run through it; cell execution never does. The prompt is piped via stdin (promptVia defaults to stdin); the command's stdout IS the digest, framed by the BEE_DIGEST delimiters per the Delegation contract's cli gather branch.
command_rules: The command must read the prompt from stdin (trailing '-' for codex exec, "$(cat)" for CLIs that only take argv prompts).
Prefer read-only/sandboxed flags (-s read-only, --sandbox, --mode plan) — a gather must not mutate the repo.
Long-running CLIs need their own timeout flags; bee does not babysit them.
Quote carefully: the command runs through a shell; bash -lc '...' keeps quoting sane for $(cat).
_doc.mixing: You can mix shapes freely per slot: here claude.extraction stays a native model (cheap + fast), while generation/review fan out to external CLIs, and codex.review uses the codex CLI itself. null slots stay prompt-budget.

examples_shown.claude.generation: Gemini via the agy CLI, plan mode, sandboxed, 30m print timeout.
examples_shown.claude.review: Claude Opus via the opencode CLI, plan agent.
examples_shown.codex.review: codex exec read-only with high reasoning effort, prompt from stdin ('-').

_doc.herding: The cli slots above and herding.agent_command are NOT the same seam: cli-shaped model/tier slots are GATHER-ONLY (file hunts, scans, reviews, advisor consults — never cell execution), while herding.agent_command is the WRITE-WORK executor for `bee herding run` / `--continue` and `bee herding wave` — a real cell-execution worker in its own worktree. Token 0 is the herdr agent kind (21 kinds, no bee-side allow-list), passed straight through; the rest is that agent's own argv — here a non-claude example, codex with its own model flag. A THIRD model-slot shape, `{ "kind": "herding" }` (CELL-ONLY, the mirror of the cli slots above), routes that slot's cell execution through `bee herding run` automatically — not shown in this sample, and not something a repo without herding.agent_command configured should turn on; an optional "agent": "<name>" on that same shape (herd-registry D1/D2) looks the name up in an optional herding.agents map (name -> argv token array, same validation as agent_command — shown live in the herding block below: claude-sonnet and agy-flash) instead of the global agent_command default; an unknown name refuses, listing every registry key. The registry is inert until a slot, --agent flag, or string agent_command names an entry — safe to keep in every repo. A herd name always means the pane transport — it never touches the cli slots above, and a cli slot can never name a herd. Canonical doc: bee-herding/references/operational-invariants.md. OPERATIONAL RULES (live-proven 2026-08-20): the spawn survives a booting shell (agent start retries agent_pane_busy up to 10 times ~1s apart); the brief is never typed into the pane — it is written to <mailbox>/brief-N.txt and the agent receives a one-line pointer, resent until the pane text echoes it (30 attempts ~1s; herdr's ready flags fire before some agents accept input); a run that fails keeps its pane as forensics, a run that succeeds closes it. Put each kind's auto-approve flag in its herd entry (claude: --permission-mode bypassPermissions; agy: --dangerously-skip-permissions) — an agent that stops to ask permission mid-run stalls until the idle-timeout. NEVER type into a live worker pane: a human keystroke hijacks the agent's turn and the brief goes unanswered.
